  FROM turbine_faults f
  JOIN turbines t ON t.turbine_id = f.turbine_id
 -- Faulted AS OF the end of the window; see the note on the region dashboard.
 WHERE f.started_at <= $__timeTo()::timestamptz
   AND (f.resolved_at IS NULL OR f.resolved_at > $__timeTo()::timestamptz)
   AND t.plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
   AND t.turbine_id::text LIKE '$turbine';

panels.title: Turbine layout — $plant
panels.description:
Auto-zooms to the plant (view = 'fit'), so you can see the actual grid: rows spaced 8 rotor diameters along the prevailing wind, columns 5 across it, and every odd row STAGGERED half a spacing sideways so the machine ahead of you is never directly ahead it. Markers are sized by output and coloured by performance ratio — a faulted machine shows up red in an otherwise green array, and its GRID POSITION is right there.

TWO ARROWS, ONE ANGLE. Parked off the flank of the array is a pair of route arrows
joined nose-to-tail, and the angle between their shafts is the whole point:

  LIGHT GREY = the plant's LAYOUT AXIS, the bearing its grid was built on.
  BLUE       = the WIND now blowing over the plant, springing from the grey arrow's tip.

When they run nearly straight, the array is taking the wind head-on down its wide
spacing and wake losses are at their lowest. When they form an elbow, the wind has swung
off the axis the array was designed for and rows begin to shadow each other. The blue arrow's LENGTH is a BOUNDED indicator of speed: 0.30 to 0.55 of the array length
as wind runs 0 to 25 m/s. This is a deliberate trade and worth stating plainly, because
earlier revisions made length strictly proportional to speed. This panel exists to show
the ANGLE, which needs both shafts comparable in length AND inside the fitted extent; a
strictly proportional arrow across a 12x speed range can satisfy neither — at the fleet
median it drew 111 m against a 1311 m axis arrow, an unreadable stub. Exact speed is in
the `wind_ms` tooltip field and on the wind timeline below. `misalignment_deg` in the tooltip is that angle as a
number, 0 (straight down the rows) to 90 (straight across them).

WHY THE GREY ARROW SOMETIMES POINTS THE 'WRONG' WAY. A grid axis is a LINE, not a
heading: rows spaced along 290 degrees are equally spaced along 110. Drawing the grey
arrow always at `grid_bearing_deg` meant that whenever the wind ran the other way down
that same axis, the blue arrow doubled back over the grey one and the angle was
unreadable — measured on this fleet, a plant with `grid_bearing_deg` 290 and wind toward
96 put the two shafts 194 degrees apart and overlapping. So the grey arrow is drawn in
whichever of its two senses FACES the wind. The tooltip carries both `grid_bearing_deg`
(the canonical layout bearing, never altered) and `axis_drawn_deg` (the sense actually
drawn), so the flip is explicit rather than mysterious.

That choice is what guarantees the picture is always readable: verified exhaustively over
all 5184 combinations of grid bearing and wind bearing at 5-degree steps, the on-screen
angle never exceeds 90 degrees, always equals the true misalignment against the axis, and
`axis_drawn_deg` is always one of the two real axis directions — never an invented one.

A SINGLE WIND ARROW, not one per turbine. Grafana's route layer renders only its FIRST
frame and joins all of that frame's points into one line (`routeLayer.tsx`:
`break; // Only the first frame for now!`), so every route arrow costs its own layer and
query. Per-turbine arrows therefore meant one layer per turbine and a hard ceiling;
collapsing to one plant-level arrow removes the ceiling entirely and makes the
array-versus-wind angle the thing you actually read. Per-turbine inflow is still
available as a timeline below.

TWO POINTS PER ARROW. Grafana draws one arrowhead PER SEGMENT, so a three-point route
grows a second head halfway down its own shaft. Two points give one clean head.

The bearing is a genuine CIRCULAR MEAN over the plant's turbines, from the unit-vector
component sums in cagg_wind_hourly — there is no correct way to average a bearing
arithmetically. The tooltip carries both `wind_from_deg` (the meteorological convention:
where the wind comes FROM) and `wind_toward_deg` (where it is going, which is where the
head points), because an arrow drawn 180 degrees out looks entirely plausible.
`steadiness` is the mean resultant length, 0-1; below 0.01 the arrow is suppressed
rather than pointing somewhere invented, and the grey axis still draws on its own.

Everything reads over a 3-HOUR TRAILING WINDOW rather than the single latest bucket,
including the turbine markers. Turbines commissioned by 12_acid_expand_plant.sql lag the
fleet by one bucket, and an equality join on MAX(bucket) dropped them outright: the plant
map showed 8 of 12 turbines and the ACID expansion demo could not display the machines it
had just added.

The grey arrow's anchor is offset perpendicular to the grid axis by 1.35x the array's
ACROSS extent so it never lands on a turbine marker (measured clearance 258-391 m). That
extent is decomposed from each turbine's offset into along-axis and across-axis
components rather than taken as a radius, because the array is deliberately elongated —
rows 8 rotor diameters apart downwind, columns 5 across — and a radius overshoots the
short flank and parks the arrow outside the layout entirely.

MAP VIEW: `allLayers: false` with `layer: "Turbines"` — pinned to one always-populated
layer. An earlier revision used `allLayers: true` so the fit would frame the arrows; that
is what broke fit-to-data on this panel. grafana/grafana#89777: a geomap with a basemap
plus at least one additional layer stays zoomed out instead of fitting. Observed on
13.1.1 — this panel fits with the layer pinned and does not with `allLayers: true`.

Because the fit only sees the Turbines layer, BOTH ARROWS ARE ANCHORED INSIDE THE ARRAY
FOOTPRINT, nudged a quarter of the array's across-extent off centre so the vertex does not
sit on the middle turbine. That is a constraint, not a preference: overlays parked outside
the pinned layer's extent cannot be rescued with padding, because padding scales an
elongated bounding box proportionally. Swept through all 36 wind bearings, an outside
anchor left 9-11 of 38 points beyond the viewport at every padding from 20 to 60; the
inside anchor gives 38/38, verified on both plants.

Also note: if the queries return NO rows, the fit does not run at all — Grafana guards on
an empty extent — and the map sits at centre 0,0 zoom 1, which looks exactly like "fit is
broken". An unresolved dashboard variable interpolates as empty and `LIKE ''` matches
nothing, so check for rows before suspecting the view config.

EXPERIMENT — a no-op `organize` transformation is attached to this panel, and to no
other. It is not here for the data. It tests whether the initial "fit to data" zoom
failing on load is a timing problem: grafana/grafana#76599 reports that a panel with a
transformation receives its data twice (once untransformed, once transformed), and the
second delivery would arrive with the map already created, re-triggering the fit that
the first pass skipped. Reproduced on Grafana 13.1.1 AND 13.1.3.

If the initial zoom is correct on this panel and still wrong on wind-4-turbine, the
cause is timing and this is the workaround. If both are still wrong, remove this —
it earns nothing and an unexplained transformation in a teaching file is a cost.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT t.name                                     AS turbine,
       t.turbine_id::text                            AS turbine_id,
       t.plant_id::text                              AS plant_id,
       t.grid_row, t.grid_col,
       ST_Y(t.location::geometry)                    AS latitude,
       ST_X(t.location::geometry)                    AS longitude,
       ROUND(h.avg_power_kw::numeric,0)              AS power_kw,
       ROUND(h.performance_ratio_pct::numeric,1)     AS performance_ratio_pct,
       ROUND(h.avg_wake_loss_pct::numeric,1)         AS wake_loss_pct,
       COALESCE(af.fault_type, 'none')               AS active_fault
  FROM turbines t
  -- Each turbine's most recent hourly row, NOT a join pinned to the fleet-wide
  -- MAX(bucket). Turbines commissioned by 12_acid_expand_plant.sql lag the fleet by
  -- one bucket, and an equality join on that bucket dropped them from the map
  -- entirely -- the ACID expansion demo could not show the turbines it had just
  -- added. LEFT JOIN so a turbine with no telemetry at all still gets a marker.
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT h.avg_power_kw, h.performance_ratio_pct, h.avg_wake_loss_pct
      FROM v_turbine_hourly h
     WHERE h.turbine_id = t.turbine_id
       AND h.bucket > (SELECT MAX(bucket) FROM cagg_turbine_power_hourly
              WHERE bucket <= $__timeTo()::timestamptz)
                      - INTERVAL '3 hours'
     ORDER BY h.bucket DESC
     LIMIT 1
  ) h ON true
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT f.fault_type FROM turbine_faults f
     WHERE f.turbine_id = t.turbine_id AND f.resolved_at IS NULL
     ORDER BY f.severity DESC LIMIT 1) af ON true
 WHERE t.plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
   AND t.turbine_id::text LIKE '$turbine'
 ORDER BY t.grid_row, t.grid_col;

WITH p AS (
  SELECT plant_id, plant_name, center_location, grid_bearing_deg
    FROM plants
   WHERE plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
),
-- Decompose each turbine's offset from the plant centre into components ALONG and
-- ACROSS the grid axis. A plain radius will not do: the array is deliberately
-- elongated (rows 8 rotor diameters apart downwind, columns 5 across, odd rows
  -- staggered half a spacing).
e AS (
  SELECT p.plant_id,
         COALESCE(MAX(ABS(ST_Distance(p.center_location, t.location)
                     * COS(ST_Azimuth(p.center_location, t.location)
                           - RADIANS(p.grid_bearing_deg)))), 400.0) AS along_m,
         COALESCE(MAX(ABS(ST_Distance(p.center_location, t.location)
                     * SIN(ST_Azimuth(p.center_location, t.location)
                           - RADIANS(p.grid_bearing_deg)))), 400.0) AS across_m
    FROM p
    LEFT JOIN turbines t
           ON t.plant_id = p.plant_id
          -- ST_Azimuth is undefined for coincident points and returns NULL, which
          -- would propagate through COS/SIN/MAX and erase the overlay.
          AND ST_Distance(p.center_location, t.location) > 0
   GROUP BY p.plant_id
),
w AS (
  SELECT h.plant_id,
         SUM(h.dir_sin_sum)                                                 AS dir_sin_sum,
         SUM(h.dir_cos_sum)                                                 AS dir_cos_sum,
         SUM(h.readings)                                                    AS readings,
         SUM(h.avg_free_wind_ms * h.readings) / NULLIF(SUM(h.readings), 0)   AS wind_ms
    FROM cagg_wind_hourly h
   -- A 3-hour trailing window rather than the single latest bucket: turbines
   -- commissioned by 12_acid_expand_plant.sql lag the fleet by one bucket, and
   -- pinning to MAX(bucket) drops them from the average.
   WHERE h.bucket > (SELECT MAX(bucket) FROM cagg_wind_hourly
              WHERE bucket <= $__timeTo()::timestamptz) - INTERVAL '3 hours'
     AND h.plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
   GROUP BY h.plant_id
  -- Suppress the wind arrow when the plant's wind boxed the compass: the resultant
  -- collapses and ATAN2(0,0) would return a confident due north.
  HAVING SQRT(SUM(h.dir_sin_sum)^2 + SUM(h.dir_cos_sum)^2) >= 0.01 * SUM(h.readings)
),
a AS (
  SELECT p.plant_id,
         p.plant_name,
         p.grid_bearing_deg,
         e.along_m,
         w.wind_ms, w.dir_sin_sum, w.dir_cos_sum, w.readings,
         MOD((DEGREES(ATAN2(w.dir_sin_sum, w.dir_cos_sum)) + 540.0)::numeric,
             360.0)::float8                                  AS wind_toward_deg,
         -- WHICH WAY TO DRAW THE GREY ARROW. A grid axis is a LINE, not a heading:
         -- rows spaced along 290 degrees are equally spaced along 110. Drawing it
         -- always at grid_bearing_deg meant that when the wind ran the other way down
         -- the same axis, the blue arrow doubled back over the grey one and the angle
         -- was unreadable. Pick the sense that faces the wind; with no wind reading,
         -- fall back to grid_bearing_deg unchanged.
         CASE
           WHEN w.dir_sin_sum IS NULL THEN p.grid_bearing_deg
           WHEN LEAST(ABS(MOD((DEGREES(ATAN2(w.dir_sin_sum, w.dir_cos_sum)) + 540.0)::numeric,
                              360.0)::float8 - p.grid_bearing_deg),
                      360.0 - ABS(MOD((DEGREES(ATAN2(w.dir_sin_sum, w.dir_cos_sum)) + 540.0)::numeric,
                                      360.0)::float8 - p.grid_bearing_deg)) <= 90.0
             THEN p.grid_bearing_deg
           ELSE MOD((p.grid_bearing_deg + 180.0)::numeric, 360.0)::float8
         END                                                 AS axis_drawn_deg,
         -- Anchor the pair INSIDE the array footprint, nudged a quarter of the way
         -- out toward one flank so it does not sit exactly on the centre turbine.
         -- Keeping it inside is what lets the map fit to the TURBINES layer alone and
         -- still frame both arrows -- verified for every wind bearing, both plants.
         -- p is joined here, NOT read with a scalar subquery: `(SELECT ... FROM p)`
         -- raised "more than one row returned by a subquery" the moment $plant
         -- matched more than one plant.
         ST_Project(p.center_location, e.across_m * 0.25,
                    RADIANS(p.grid_bearing_deg + 90.0))       AS anchor
    FROM p
    JOIN e ON e.plant_id = p.plant_id
    -- LEFT so the layout axis still draws on a plant with no usable wind reading.
    LEFT JOIN w ON w.plant_id = p.plant_id
)
-- THE PLANT'S LAYOUT AXIS, in light grey. The blue wind arrow springs from this
-- arrow's TIP, so the angle between the two shafts IS the misalignment between the
-- array and the wind now blowing over it.
SELECT s.seq                                     AS point_seq,
       a.plant_name,
       ST_Y(g.pt::geometry)                      AS latitude,
       ST_X(g.pt::geometry)                      AS longitude,
       ROUND(a.grid_bearing_deg::numeric, 0)     AS grid_bearing_deg,
       ROUND(a.axis_drawn_deg::numeric, 0)       AS axis_drawn_deg,
       ROUND((a.along_m * 0.80)::numeric, 0)     AS axis_len_m
  FROM a
  -- TWO points, so Grafana draws exactly ONE arrowhead. It draws one per SEGMENT, so
  -- a three-point route grows a second head halfway down its own shaft.
  -- No MOD on the azimuth: ST_Project is periodic in it, and MOD(double precision,
  -- numeric) has no overload anyway.
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL (VALUES (1), (2)) s(seq)
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT CASE s.seq
             WHEN 1 THEN ST_Project(a.anchor, a.along_m * 0.40,
                                    RADIANS(a.axis_drawn_deg + 180.0))
             ELSE        ST_Project(a.anchor, a.along_m * 0.40,
                                    RADIANS(a.axis_drawn_deg))
           END AS pt
  ) g
 ORDER BY a.plant_name, s.seq;

WITH p AS (
  SELECT plant_id, plant_name, center_location, grid_bearing_deg
    FROM plants
   WHERE plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
),
-- Decompose each turbine's offset from the plant centre into components ALONG and
-- ACROSS the grid axis. A plain radius will not do: the array is deliberately
-- elongated (rows 8 rotor diameters apart downwind, columns 5 across, odd rows
  -- staggered half a spacing).
e AS (
  SELECT p.plant_id,
         COALESCE(MAX(ABS(ST_Distance(p.center_location, t.location)
                     * COS(ST_Azimuth(p.center_location, t.location)
                           - RADIANS(p.grid_bearing_deg)))), 400.0) AS along_m,
         COALESCE(MAX(ABS(ST_Distance(p.center_location, t.location)
                     * SIN(ST_Azimuth(p.center_location, t.location)
                           - RADIANS(p.grid_bearing_deg)))), 400.0) AS across_m
    FROM p
    LEFT JOIN turbines t
           ON t.plant_id = p.plant_id
          -- ST_Azimuth is undefined for coincident points and returns NULL, which
          -- would propagate through COS/SIN/MAX and erase the overlay.
          AND ST_Distance(p.center_location, t.location) > 0
   GROUP BY p.plant_id
),
w AS (
  SELECT h.plant_id,
         SUM(h.dir_sin_sum)                                                 AS dir_sin_sum,
         SUM(h.dir_cos_sum)                                                 AS dir_cos_sum,
         SUM(h.readings)                                                    AS readings,
         SUM(h.avg_free_wind_ms * h.readings) / NULLIF(SUM(h.readings), 0)   AS wind_ms
    FROM cagg_wind_hourly h
   -- A 3-hour trailing window rather than the single latest bucket: turbines
   -- commissioned by 12_acid_expand_plant.sql lag the fleet by one bucket, and
   -- pinning to MAX(bucket) drops them from the average.
   WHERE h.bucket > (SELECT MAX(bucket) FROM cagg_wind_hourly
              WHERE bucket <= $__timeTo()::timestamptz) - INTERVAL '3 hours'
     AND h.plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
   GROUP BY h.plant_id
  -- Suppress the wind arrow when the plant's wind boxed the compass: the resultant
  -- collapses and ATAN2(0,0) would return a confident due north.
  HAVING SQRT(SUM(h.dir_sin_sum)^2 + SUM(h.dir_cos_sum)^2) >= 0.01 * SUM(h.readings)
),
a AS (
  SELECT p.plant_id,
         p.plant_name,
         p.grid_bearing_deg,
         e.along_m,
         w.wind_ms, w.dir_sin_sum, w.dir_cos_sum, w.readings,
         MOD((DEGREES(ATAN2(w.dir_sin_sum, w.dir_cos_sum)) + 540.0)::numeric,
             360.0)::float8                                  AS wind_toward_deg,
         -- WHICH WAY TO DRAW THE GREY ARROW. A grid axis is a LINE, not a heading:
         -- rows spaced along 290 degrees are equally spaced along 110. Drawing it
         -- always at grid_bearing_deg meant that when the wind ran the other way down
         -- the same axis, the blue arrow doubled back over the grey one and the angle
         -- was unreadable. Pick the sense that faces the wind; with no wind reading,
         -- fall back to grid_bearing_deg unchanged.
         CASE
           WHEN w.dir_sin_sum IS NULL THEN p.grid_bearing_deg
           WHEN LEAST(ABS(MOD((DEGREES(ATAN2(w.dir_sin_sum, w.dir_cos_sum)) + 540.0)::numeric,
                              360.0)::float8 - p.grid_bearing_deg),
                      360.0 - ABS(MOD((DEGREES(ATAN2(w.dir_sin_sum, w.dir_cos_sum)) + 540.0)::numeric,
                                      360.0)::float8 - p.grid_bearing_deg)) <= 90.0
             THEN p.grid_bearing_deg
           ELSE MOD((p.grid_bearing_deg + 180.0)::numeric, 360.0)::float8
         END                                                 AS axis_drawn_deg,
         -- Anchor the pair INSIDE the array footprint, nudged a quarter of the way
         -- out toward one flank so it does not sit exactly on the centre turbine.
         -- Keeping it inside is what lets the map fit to the TURBINES layer alone and
         -- still frame both arrows -- verified for every wind bearing, both plants.
         -- p is joined here, NOT read with a scalar subquery: `(SELECT ... FROM p)`
         -- raised "more than one row returned by a subquery" the moment $plant
         -- matched more than one plant.
         ST_Project(p.center_location, e.across_m * 0.25,
                    RADIANS(p.grid_bearing_deg + 90.0))       AS anchor
    FROM p
    JOIN e ON e.plant_id = p.plant_id
    -- LEFT so the layout axis still draws on a plant with no usable wind reading.
    LEFT JOIN w ON w.plant_id = p.plant_id
)
-- THE WIND OVER THIS PLANT, in blue: ONE arrow springing from the tip of the grey
-- layout arrow. The angle between the shafts is how far the wind has swung off the
-- axis the array was built for.
SELECT s.seq                                     AS point_seq,
       a.plant_name,
       ST_Y(g.pt::geometry)                      AS latitude,
       ST_X(g.pt::geometry)                      AS longitude,
       ROUND(a.wind_ms::numeric, 1)              AS wind_ms,
       ROUND(MOD((DEGREES(ATAN2(a.dir_sin_sum, a.dir_cos_sum)) + 360.0)::numeric,
                 360.0), 0)                      AS wind_from_deg,
       ROUND(a.wind_toward_deg::numeric, 0)      AS wind_toward_deg,
       ROUND(a.grid_bearing_deg::numeric, 0)     AS grid_bearing_deg,
       ROUND(a.axis_drawn_deg::numeric, 0)       AS axis_drawn_deg,
       -- The angle you actually SEE between the two shafts, which by construction is
       -- also the misalignment against the grid axis: 0 = wind straight down the rows,
       -- 90 = straight across them. Folded to 0-90 because the axis is a line.
       ROUND(LEAST(ABS(a.wind_toward_deg - a.axis_drawn_deg),
                   360.0 - ABS(a.wind_toward_deg - a.axis_drawn_deg))::numeric,
             1)                                  AS misalignment_deg,
       ROUND((SQRT(a.dir_sin_sum^2 + a.dir_cos_sum^2)
              / NULLIF(a.readings, 0))::numeric, 2) AS steadiness,
       -- Length is a BOUNDED indicator of speed, not a strictly proportional one:
       -- 0.30 to 0.55 of the array length as wind runs 0 to 25 m/s. That is a
       -- deliberate trade. This panel exists to show the ANGLE, which needs the two
       -- shafts to stay comparable in length and inside the fitted extent; a strictly
       -- proportional arrow over a 12x speed range cannot do both. Exact speed is in
       -- `wind_ms` here and on the wind timeline below.
       ROUND((a.along_m * (0.30 + 0.25 * LEAST(a.wind_ms, 25.0) / 25.0))::numeric, 0)
                                                 AS len_m
  FROM a
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL (VALUES (1), (2)) s(seq)
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT CASE s.seq
             -- Start a short way PAST the grey arrow's tip: the small gap keeps the
             -- shafts from overlapping while holding their vertex in one place, which
             -- is what makes the angle legible.
             WHEN 1 THEN ST_Project(
                           ST_Project(a.anchor, a.along_m * 0.40,
                                      RADIANS(a.axis_drawn_deg)),
                           a.along_m * 0.06, RADIANS(a.axis_drawn_deg))
             ELSE        ST_Project(
                           ST_Project(
                             ST_Project(a.anchor, a.along_m * 0.40,
                                        RADIANS(a.axis_drawn_deg)),
                             a.along_m * 0.06, RADIANS(a.axis_drawn_deg)),
                           a.along_m * (0.30 + 0.25 * LEAST(a.wind_ms, 25.0) / 25.0),
                           RADIANS(a.wind_toward_deg))
           END AS pt
  ) g
 -- No wind reading means no arrow at all, rather than a zero-length stub.
 WHERE a.wind_toward_deg IS NOT NULL
 ORDER BY a.plant_name, s.seq;

panels.title: Turbine detail — as of window end
panels.description:
Per-turbine metrics with grid position and the fault answer key alongside. Sort by performance_ratio_pct to rank suspects, then check active_fault to see whether the ranking was right.

Note how grid_row correlates with wake_loss_pct but NOT with performance_ratio_pct — wake is a property of position, degradation is a property of the machine. Separating the two is the point of storing both.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT t.name                                     AS turbine,
       t.turbine_id::text                            AS turbine_id,
       t.plant_id::text                              AS plant_id,
       t.grid_row, t.grid_col,
       ROUND(h.avg_power_kw::numeric,0)              AS power_kw,
       ROUND(h.avg_expected_power_kw::numeric,0)     AS expected_kw,
       ROUND(h.performance_ratio_pct::numeric,1)     AS performance_ratio_pct,
       ROUND(h.capacity_factor_pct::numeric,1)       AS capacity_factor_pct,
       ROUND(h.avg_wake_loss_pct::numeric,1)         AS wake_loss_pct,
       COALESCE(af.fault_type, '—')                  AS active_fault,
       CASE WHEN af.detected_at IS NULL AND af.fault_type IS NOT NULL
              THEN 'UNDIAGNOSED' END                 AS status
  FROM turbines t
  JOIN v_turbine_hourly h ON h.turbine_id = t.turbine_id AND h.bucket = (SELECT MAX(bucket) FROM cagg_turbine_power_hourly
              WHERE bucket <= $__timeTo()::timestamptz)
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT f.fault_type, f.detected_at FROM turbine_faults f
     WHERE f.turbine_id = t.turbine_id AND f.resolved_at IS NULL
     ORDER BY f.severity DESC LIMIT 1) af ON true
 WHERE t.plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
   AND t.turbine_id::text LIKE '$turbine'
 ORDER BY h.performance_ratio_pct;

panels.title: Expected vs actual output  —  the gap IS the fault  (tier-selected)
panels.description:
Two traces summed across the plant's turbines: what the measured wind should have produced, and what was produced. They sit on top of each other for a healthy plant, and the gap between them IS the degradation — gradual opening is soiling or blade wear, a step is a pitch fault or curtailment.

Tier-selected over the turbine daily aggregate, the turbine hourly aggregate and raw. Six UNION branches here rather than three, because each tier contributes both metrics — the gates still leave exactly two alive.

targets.rawSql:
-- One point per day or coarser: the daily rollup already has it.
  SELECT day AS time,
         'expected (kW)' AS metric,
         ROUND((SUM(avg_expected_power_kw))::numeric, 1) AS value
    FROM cagg_turbine_power_daily
   WHERE $__timeFilter(day)
       AND plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
       AND turbine_id::text LIKE '$turbine'
       AND $__interval_ms >= 86400000
   GROUP BY day
  UNION ALL
  -- One point per day or coarser: the daily rollup already has it.
  SELECT day AS time,
         'actual (kW)' AS metric,
         ROUND((SUM(avg_power_kw))::numeric, 1) AS value
    FROM cagg_turbine_power_daily
   WHERE $__timeFilter(day)
       AND plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
       AND turbine_id::text LIKE '$turbine'
       AND $__interval_ms >= 86400000
   GROUP BY day
  UNION ALL
  -- One point per hour or coarser: the hourly rollup is fine enough.
  SELECT bucket AS time,
         'expected (kW)' AS metric,
         ROUND((SUM(avg_expected_power_kw))::numeric, 1) AS value
    FROM cagg_turbine_power_hourly
   WHERE $__timeFilter(bucket)
       AND plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
       AND turbine_id::text LIKE '$turbine'
       AND $__interval_ms >= 3600000
       AND $__interval_ms <  86400000
   GROUP BY bucket
  UNION ALL
  -- One point per hour or coarser: the hourly rollup is fine enough.
  SELECT bucket AS time,
         'actual (kW)' AS metric,
         ROUND((SUM(avg_power_kw))::numeric, 1) AS value
    FROM cagg_turbine_power_hourly
   WHERE $__timeFilter(bucket)
       AND plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
       AND turbine_id::text LIKE '$turbine'
       AND $__interval_ms >= 3600000
       AND $__interval_ms <  86400000
   GROUP BY bucket
  UNION ALL
  -- Finer than an hour: only the raw samples carry more detail.
  SELECT time_bucket('15 minutes', time) AS time,
         'expected (kW)' AS metric,
         ROUND((SUM(expected_power_kw))::numeric, 1) AS value
    FROM power_generation
   WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
       AND plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
       AND turbine_id::text LIKE '$turbine'
       AND $__interval_ms <  3600000
   GROUP BY time_bucket('15 minutes', time)
  UNION ALL
  -- Finer than an hour: only the raw samples carry more detail.
  SELECT time_bucket('15 minutes', time) AS time,
         'actual (kW)' AS metric,
         ROUND((SUM(power_kw))::numeric, 1) AS value
    FROM power_generation
   WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
       AND plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
       AND turbine_id::text LIKE '$turbine'
       AND $__interval_ms <  3600000
   GROUP BY time_bucket('15 minutes', time)
 ORDER BY time;

panels.title: Fault history for this plant  (the answer key)
panels.description: turbine_faults for the selected plant. `detected_at` deliberately lags `started_at` — a gradual fault runs for weeks before anyone notices, and closing that gap is what the monitoring is for. Rows with no detected date are still undiagnosed.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT t.name                                          AS turbine,
       f.fault_type,
       ROUND((f.severity*100)::numeric,1)                 AS severity_pct,
       f.ramp_days,
       ROUND(((1-turbine_health(t.turbine_id, $__timeTo()::timestamptz))*100)::numeric,1) AS derate_now_pct,
       f.started_at,
       f.detected_at,
       CASE WHEN f.detected_at IS NULL THEN NULL
            ELSE (f.detected_at::date - f.started_at::date) END        AS days_to_detect,
       f.resolved_at,
       f.notes
  FROM turbine_faults f
  JOIN turbines t ON t.turbine_id = f.turbine_id
 WHERE t.plant_id = NULLIF('$plant','')::uuid
   AND t.turbine_id::text LIKE '$turbine'
 ORDER BY f.resolved_at NULLS FIRST, f.severity DESC;
